The test image shows soybean stems with dark brown/purplish-brown linear discoloration running along the stem, with green pods nearby. Key features: stem lesions, dark brown-purple coloration, hairy stem surface.

Top candidates: Anthracnose, Phomopsis, Diaporthe, Brown_Stem_Rot, Charcoal_Rot. Let me compare reference images.
Let me view one more reference to differentiate between Anthracnose and Diaporthe.

**Visual analysis summary:**
- **Affected part**: Stem/petiole (close-up, elevated — not at soil level)
- **Coloration**: Dark brown to purplish-brown linear discoloration running along the stem length
- **Context**: Green pods visible — mid-to-late season
- **Texture**: Smooth uniform discoloration, no distinct pycnidia spots or acervuli visible

**Candidate elimination:**
- **Septoria/Frogeye/Cercospora**: Leaf diseases — ruled out
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Shows internal browning + interveinal leaf chlorosis, not external purple-brown stem — ruled out
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Dry grey/tan stems at soil level late-season — ruled out
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reddish lesions at hypocotyl/soil line — ruled out
- **Phomopsis**: Circular pycnidia spots on pods — not matching
- **Anthracnose**: Dark acervuli spots on pods/shriveled late-season stems — not matching well
- **Diaporthe**: Dark brown stem cankers running linearly along stems, consistent with mid-season with green pods present — **best match**. The Diaporthe reference (upper right panel) shows dark brown/purplish elongated stem lesions that closely match the test image's pattern.
